clue.text: Gents leading light, Marsh

indicators.note: leading means the first piece goes in front of the next one

parts.note: the gents is a men's lavatory, slang bog in Britain
to light on something is to land or alight on it

explanation.surface: A man in the lead, a guiding light, is called Marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The gents is a men's toilet, called a bog in British slang; 'leading' puts it first. Light is the verb, to come down and settle.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggy ground is wetland, a synonym for a marsh or swamp.

clue.text: Midge possibly lacks nitrogen, having started with topping of banana split

indicators.note: this places the first piece at the start, before the rest
the topping is the first letter, at the top of the down entry
lacks means a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a midge is an example of an insect
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A midge, minus its nitrogen, began on top of a banana split dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banana split' looks like a dessert, but split is the definition; 'lacks' drops nitrogen from the midge's class.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two halves, to split.

clue.text: Sombre, grand — like something from a cotton mill!

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand

parts.words: like something from a cotton mill
parts.note: a cotton mill is full of looms, so loomy is jocularly like one

explanation.surface: Dark and imposing, like an old Lancashire cotton mill.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOMY is a made-up adjective: like a loom, the weaving machine of cotton mills.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and sombre both mean dark, dismal or melancholy.

clue.text: "Catwalk Al" in IT yearly renders lime property

indicators.note: renders means gives out, so the letters are delivered from within the words

explanation.surface: A fashion model called Al is in IT every year, making lime green.
explanation.walkthrough: Lime looks like a colour or fruit, but it is the chemical calcium oxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime is a strong base, so its chemical character is being alkaline, the opposite of acidity.

clue.text: Obligation to accept independent book entry

indicators.note: accepting means taking the letter in, so it goes inside

parts.note: a debt is a financial obligation

explanation.surface: An obligation to take on an independent publisher's listing.
explanation.walkthrough: Book here means an account book.
explanation.definitionFit: In bookkeeping, a sum recorded as owed is entered on the debit side of the ledger.

clue.text: Local funny papers drop

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or peculiar, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: ff is the abbreviation for folios or following pages, taken as papers

explanation.surface: A local comic paper is being discontinued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' shuffles the five letters of the first word; papers are folios, abbreviated ff.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a plan is to abandon or cancel it, the phrasal verb meaning exactly that.

clue.text: Jaguar, say, almost without assistance on back road somewhere in Europe

parts.note: a jaguar is an example of a big cat

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to do something alone is to do it without help

indicators.note: on back means the word turns around and comes after

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest road, written AI

explanation.surface: A Jaguar car, nearly unaided, travels a back road through a European region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' clips the last letter; 'on back' turns the A1, Britain's main north-south trunk road, and places it after.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of north-east Spain around Barcelona is a place in Europe.

clue.text: Hank's vulgar face about to go

indicators.note: to go means that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: clock is slang for a face
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Hank has an ugly face that is about to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Hank looks like a name; it is a coil of hair or yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: A hank of hair is a lock, a tress.

clue.text: Vocal work or a chamber work incorporating a round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: incorporating means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: a trio is a piece of chamber music for three players
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A choral piece, or a chamber composition with a round included.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIO takes in O to give TORIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale musical setting for voices, often religious, like Handel's Messiah.

clue.text: Had advance knowledge of elevated king in start again

indicators.note: in a down answer, elevated means the word reads upwards
in means the letter is placed inside the next piece

parts.note: to renew is to begin again
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Somebody knew in advance about a raised king making a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'elevated' reads the little word upwards; 'in' puts the king inside the fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreknow is to know beforehand, so its past tense is having advance knowledge.

clue.text: Hit required outside temperature for animals

indicators.note: the blow is wanted round the other piece, so it wraps it

parts.note: to sock someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: A blow was needed outside because of the heat, for the sake of the creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required outside' sets SOCK around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm animals kept collectively are livestock, often just called stock.

clue.text: Club with hot and cold shock device for those unfit to walk

definitions.text: device for those unfit to walk

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
H stands for hot on taps
C stands for cold on taps
a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: A club armed with hot and cold electric-shock gadgets for invalids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks electrical but is a mop of hair. A bath chair is an old hooded wheelchair named after the spa town of Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath chair was a wheeled chair pushed along for invalids who could not walk.

clue.text: Appealing about Penny and Grant's 12 24 and 19 as well as 6 9 and 20

indicators.note: about means the first word is placed around the following pieces

parts.note: comely means pleasant to look at, appealing
to let is to grant or allow

explanation.surface: An attractive couple, Penny and Grant, are tangled up in a list of cross-references.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the appealing word round the coin and the grant. The cross-references read 'hook, line and sinker' and 'lock, stock and barrel', both idioms for entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowing it hook, line and sinker, or taking lock, stock and barrel, both mean totally, without reservation.

clue.text: Peg wobbled, being topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: shook means trembled or wobbled

explanation.surface: Peg trembled, having stripped to the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name; it is a hanging peg. 'being topless' drops the S of SHOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat hook is a peg on which things are hung.

clue.text: "Prime motivator" uses electric source with high-pitched sound to stifle resistance

parts.note: the mains is the household electricity supply

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the letter is surrounded

parts.note: a ping is a short high ringing sound
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: The main motive force draws on the electric supply, with a whine smothering any resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: PING wraps R to give PRING.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief driving force behind something is figuratively its mainspring, after the spring driving a watch.

clue.text: Not the sort of operation Hitler went in for?

definitions.text: Not the sort of operation Hitler went in for?

parts.words: Not the sort of operation Hitler went in for
parts.note: a surgical term for a procedure without cutting, read as a military operation that does not invade a country

explanation.surface: Hitler was no stranger to military operations that crossed borders.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical procedure involving no incision is described this way, here applied to military invasion.

clue.text: Unrestricted sign banning bands on public highway?

definitions.meaning: unrestricted means with no conditions attached

definitions.text: sign banning bands on public highway?
definitions.meaning: a road sign forbidding violins and other bowed groups, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: Without strings means with no conditions, so a no-ties deal is unrestricted.

clue.text: Offer to form a union?

parts.note: a business offer to join, read as a request to marry

explanation.surface: A bid to set up a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage offer, asking someone to wed, is the classic case.

clue.text: Say "good works producing fruit"

parts.note: eg is short for for example, say
a plant is a factory or works

explanation.surface: Someone recommends that good deeds bear fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good works' looks like charity; works is a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the aubergine is a fruit, called by this name in America.

clue.text: Well just like a fall

parts.note: right means just or fair
as means like, in comparison
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: Fine, just like a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fall' hints at a stumble but is rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly fit and healthy, so it is a colourful synonym for well.

clue.text: Rogue trader at first lost weight

indicators.note: lost means that letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: a stinker is a nasty person, a rogue

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rogue trader initially lost a great deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue trader' reads as one phrase; split it. STINKER loses the T from the start of trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinker is the weight attached to a fishing line to make it sink.

clue.text: Blunder into party, turning over drum

indicators.note: turning over means the assembled letters read backwards, upwards in the grid
into means the error goes inside the other piece

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A mistake gets into the party, overturning a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts the mistake inside the party, and 'turning over' reads the whole result upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel is a cylindrical cask, a drum for holding liquid.

clue.text: Monarch's stage (revolving) erected by state

indicators.note: revolving turns the word round so its letters read backwards

parts.note: something erected is put up
PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state

explanation.surface: A king's platform keeps turning and was built by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: Monarch is a butterfly, not a king; its stage of development is wanted. 'revolving' turns the erected word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysalis is the stage a monarch butterfly passes through between caterpillar and adult.

clue.text: Fly, ship or load bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters before it go wild

explanation.surface: A fly is aboard the ship, or loads of bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges SHIPORLOAD. Fitting, as this is the fruit fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus of small fruit flies used widely in genetics research.

clue.text: Groovy thing looks back (around mid-sixties)

indicators.note: around means the reversed word wraps around the other letter
back means the word reads in reverse

parts.note: airs are looks or appearances, as in airs and graces

indicators.note: mid takes the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something groovy looks back to the mid-sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' and 'sixties' paint flower power, but a stria is a groove. AIRS read backwards gives SRIA, around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is a thin groove or ridge, so literally a grooved thing.

clue.text: Chinese distance, bearing and course

parts.note: a li is a traditional Chinese unit of length
NE, north-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A Chinese journey of some length, its direction and route.
explanation.definitionFit: A line is a route or course of travel, as a line of march.

clue.text: Base King Edward, a source of material for writers

definitions.text: a source of material for writers

parts.note: a station is a base, as in a military station
ER stands for Edward Rex, Latin for King Edward

explanation.surface: A King Edward stationed at the base supplies writers.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward suggests a potato, but gives ER (Edwardus Rex).
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling paper, pens and envelopes supplies writing materials.

clue.text: No time for old repair man to become print worker

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is dropped from the word

parts.note: a tinker was a travelling mender of pots and pans

explanation.surface: An old handyman too busy to stay retrains as a printer.
explanation.walkthrough: TINKER loses its T, the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies ink, as on a printing press or in comic art, is an inker.

clue.text: Unusual origins of Newcastle United-style English scorer

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are reordered
the origins are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A Newcastle United footballer scores in an English style unlike any other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' scrambles NU (initials from 'origins of') with STYLE. Scorer here is a composer of musical scores: Elisabeth Lutyens.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisabeth Lutyens was an English composer, someone who writes musical scores.

clue.text: Predicting the month by a range name

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August
the Urals are a mountain range in Russia, named here as one

explanation.surface: A forecaster foresees the month by a mountain range's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Augural refers to augury, the reading of omens to foretell the future.
